items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Lewis played with him and I played with him.

ctx.x: You worked with P. Ron, huh? Sure.

Did you ever, did you know Fate Marble? No. Did you ever play the riverboat? We were on the boat, from the other St. Louis. You played with Fate Marble on the riverboat. Yes, sir. Alright, now who else was in that group? Well, I know Fate was in it. See, every time I get into something like that, I'm in Lewis' place. Lewis had been on there with him. Yeah. And Lewis left. And I just got in there with him. You know, he only made one record. What is Fate? Yeah. Shall I? That's all he made, just one record. He was a…
I don't know what his name is.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: No, Fate Narrable. I just played with him on one trip. One trip, I knew.

ctx.x: Oh, Fate Narrable. I think, tell me, Erskine Tate. Erskine Tate, no. No, that's in Chicago. Yeah, yeah. No, Fate Narrable. I just played with him on one trip. One trip, I knew. You just go up the river with him. Yeah, yeah. One trip.
How long did that go? A month or so? Mm-hmm. How long? Not all summer?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: One Sunday on the boat in Louis' place. One Sunday. Just one. Something was wrong with Louis, couldn't make it. I like that play with him.

ctx.x: Oh, did you ever work with Fate Marable? Fate Marable?

One Sunday on the boat in Louis' place. One Sunday. Just one. Something was wrong with Louis, couldn't make it. I like that play with him. I was a lot of head white too. Head white man. I thought they were good musicians. Fate was, yeah, but people in the band wasn't. Who was in the band? Oh, the most of them was from St. Louis. I can't think of them long. I don't think of anyone around, not their name, any more than Fate. Remember Foots Thomas? Foots, I remember him, yeah. Walter Foots Thomas? Mm-hmm.
Who'd you hear him? He was a great big fella that used to play drums. I don't know his name.
